title: Perpendicular Slopes Walkthrough
prompt: Unpack the shortcut in the same order you would use during a timed exam.

steps.title: Read the given slope
steps.content: The line $y = 2x + 3$ has slope **2** because it is already in slope-intercept form.

steps.title: Change the sign
steps.content: Perpendicular slopes are **negative reciprocals**, so the slope becomes $-\frac{1}{2}$.

steps.title: Match the choice
steps.content: Look for a line with slope $-\frac{1}{2}$. The correct choice is **$y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 4$**.

fallback.markdown: Perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is $-1$. Starting from slope $2$, take the reciprocal to get $\frac{1}{2}$, then change the sign to get $-\frac{1}{2}$.
